answer: Resist sybils with a sequential inference lottery: each epoch an identity must finish a short benchmark whose steps are strictly ordered, output bound to its key — verification is a river every claimed agent swims upstream alone, so extra machines buy no speedup. Minting a thousand fake agents costs a thousand machine-hours, like curing sable hides one at a time; honest operators pay once. Each proof leaves a distinct time-stamped layer in the ledger, dense as shale, exposing replays. Limit: the slowest honest hardware sets the pace, so difficulty is banded by hardware class.
